actions.description: Map the reviewed native products and author-prepared inputs to portable SAS library aliases and align SAS export with the Stata working directory.

validation: Read-only metadata confirms each configured member, exact native field map and file format. The shared output location continues to match the checked `bias` basename and SAS-before-Stata order; no sample or analysis logic changes.

actions.description: Confirm the intended SAS 9.4 runtime is available in the later execution context before attempting the preparation stage.

case when (count(b.acode)>=1) then 1 else 0 end as star

issues.description: The SAS driver calls an external previous_trading_day macro and requires its output member/previous-day field before the CRSP daily join. The macro body and exact input/output behavior are not in the package or registered source closure; the date mapping cannot be treated as verified.

The supplied SAS source consumes author-prepared TRANS_ANALYST, STAR, S2, AUM, CRSP_WEIGHT, analyst-date/count tables and FIRM_CONTROLS whose exact local catalog candidates/producers are not established. IBES.RECDDET is author-documented from WRDS but lacks an exact local candidate/header. COMP.FUNDQ is a readable local candidate; among the eight source-required Firm_Controls fields, only CUSIP appears in its header. DATADATE is available as a separate candidate date field, but no supplied interval/control construction maps it to FYENDDT/NEXT_FYENDDT or the required controls. These products and their fields/history remain unresolved; the packaged CUSIP list is identifier-only, not the prepared panel.

The safe view of the original environment probe reports the SAS runtime as unverified with return code 1 and no version token. This assessment did not start SAS; the intended SAS 9.4 runtime must be confirmed in the eventual execution context.

The source uses `winsor2`; static metadata says the command is unavailable in both default and configured Stata paths. Other source-used Stata commands were found, so this is a specific addon preparation need.

review_notes: The byte-first reader screened the complete supplied SAS and Stata source and the registered documentation before any source/document display. Quoted Windows path bytes and connection/configuration blocks were masked; raw logs and helper streams remain opaque.

The field matrix records source-consumed raw fields, full exact native catalog field lists/case, and exact headers from successful one-row probes. Four complete compatible local products (IBES.DETU_EPSUS, IBES.PTGDET, CRSP.MSENAMES and CRSP.DSF) are positively routed; the probes establish readability/header compatibility, not population, value or endpoint-history coverage.

COMP.FUNDQ is a complete/readable 648-field local candidate, but the direct SAS consumer is prepared WD.Firm_Controls. Among that table's eight explicitly consumed fields only CUSIP appears in COMP.FUNDQ; DATADATE is separately present but no producer or fiscal-interval mapping is inferred.

WD.TRANS_ANALYST, WD.STAR, WD.S2, WD.AUM, WD.CRSP_WEIGHT, both analyst-date tables, the analyst-year counts and WD.Firm_Controls remain distinct author-prepared products. The datasheet's documented WRDS products provide partial upstream routes only where stated; they do not prove prepared-table construction or history.
The SAS source also reads CRSP2.MSENAMES at lines 263-265, which the frozen dependency registry did not enumerate; it is separately tracked and has a verified local native product route.

The saved handoff check confirms the SAS Stata-format export basename and directory match Stata's `bias` input and working directory; SAS preparation precedes the Stata analysis. No author SAS/model/regression/statistical execution, installation, download or source edit was performed.
